protocol.scope: Private exploratory aggregate development check after four-case orientation/correction feasibility; not confirmation, student preregistration, held-out evaluation, or acceleration evidence
protocol.selection: All eight pinned original validation inverse slices, all 24 original source/frequency blocks per slice, four parent groups; no exclusions or rank search
protocol.direction: For each method/slice, negative SUM of all 24 physical approximate block gradients, normalized by one common L2 norm; zero if norm<=1e-14
protocol.acceptance: SUM approximate Dphi + SUM all24 block error bounds <0, only if every block stability is available; otherwise retain fallback-required case
protocol.coverage: Absolute aggregate error <= SUM24 bounds +1e-12; retain all individual block errors and bound checks with the same shared aggregate direction
protocol.uncertainty: Equal-parent descriptive summaries across four parents; no IID-eight-slice or inferential coverage claim
protocol.gram_allowance: Same private feasibility formula: max(0,-lambda_min(G))+128*eps*rank*max(||H||2+||Vr||2^2,1) added to G diagonal; explicitly not a formally verified rounding enclosure

output_contract.families_or_parent_pooling: Retain parent identity; report every method and slice separately plus equal-parent descriptions

offline_verification_counts.note: All full-grid solves/SVDs are validation labels/checks, not candidate online work.

candidate_work_scope: Frozen64-POD model assemblies and reduced state/adjoint solves; rank96 spectral stability; reduced orientation responses/corrections, residuals, projections and aggregate bound. No fine receiver maps/factorizations/solves, NN or JVP are required by the candidate certificate.
limitations: Exploratory aggregate development check explicitly after the four-case orientation result; not prospective confirmation or student preregistration.
Eight correlated validation slices from four parents, not eight IID geological cases; only equal-parent descriptive summaries, no inferential coverage or generalization claim.
Ordinary floating-point Gram allowance is not a verified roundoff enclosure; no finite-step or adaptive-trajectory guarantee.
No timings or acceleration claim; retained stability-unavailable cases require fallback rather than being dropped.
